arun (PM): Heads-up — three customers asked this week for the same thing: pin model version to v1.2, ensure EU + CA availability, and a clear fallback policy if capacity is constrained. can we sketch a proposal?
lina (Support): +1 from two support cases (acme + novex). both are compliance-driven — need EU residency and version lock.
sam (Sales): also hearing from a mid-market where they want guaranteed v1.2 until end of Q3 as part of contract. they asked about failover to hosted vs degraded model.
julia (Eng-ML): technical note: v1.2 is quantized; we have a lighter v1.2-q6f and a float v1.3 candidate. fallback to v1.2-q6f is painless, but fallback to v1.3 may cause sig perf differences.
kevin (Eng-Runtime): runtime constraints: EU pool is light this week. if we pin capacity we either reserve dedicated or add routing fallback to other regions with encryption/consent gating. autoscale + spot GPUs okay but not SLA-backed.
arun (PM): launch criteria idea: 1) v1.2 pinned variant available in EU/CA; 2) documented fallback tree; 3) opt-in checkbox for cross-region fallback in contract; 4) rolling canary and perf evals. any missing?
marta (Compliance): must include data residency statement and KMS mapping for EU keys. cross-region fallback must be explicit consent; log retention controls too.
lina (Support): request: make a short support playbook for customers — when to enable fallback, how to interpret degraded outputs. keeps cs reps consistent.
julia (Eng-ML): propose fallback policy in config form:```fallback_policy: [ {condition: "eu_capacity_low", action: "route_to:eu-compatible-quant", accept_quality_drop: true}, {condition: "eu_unavailable", action: "route_to:region:us-west", require_customer_consent: true} ]```
kevin (Eng-Runtime): that config looks reasonable. we should add a soft-throttling step to avoid sudden RPS spikes during failover. also add telemetry tags: customer_id, pinned_version, fallback_reason.
sam (Sales): timeline ask from customer: need commitment within 2 weeks to include in contract. is that realistic if we do documentation + explicit consent option?
arun (PM): realistic path: (A) quick opt-in checkbox + support playbook + policy docs = 10 business days, no infra changes. (B) full reserved capacity + SLA = requires capacity planning + sales ops, ~6 weeks. callout: any customers needing SLA should be pushed to Dedicated.
marta (Compliance): approval for opt-in wording: "Customer consents to cross-region fallback for availability reasons; data will remain encrypted and access logs retained." get legal sign-off but ok to draft.
julia (Eng-ML): for (A) we can ship docs + runtime gating to prefer eu-quant within 7-10 days. I'll add perf regressions test harness for their prompts.
kevin (Eng-Runtime): I'll scope the minimal runtime flags: `--pin-version=v1.2 --fallback=eu-quant,us-west:consent --telemetry=fallback_reason`. estimate 2 dev-days for gating + 1 day for telemetry.
arun (PM): next steps: 1) julia to add perf harness + tests (deadline 3 business days) 2) kevin to prototype runtime flags (2 business days) 3) lina to draft support playbook (2 business days) 4) sam to inform customers of opt-in path and timeline (ASAP) 5) marta to coordinate legal for consent wording (3 business days). I'll track in product backlog as ticket PROD-3491.
ops-bot: deploy note — no deploys scheduled for prod-runtime in next 48h.
kevin (Eng-Runtime): noted. will branch feature flag and open PR; tagging with PROD-3491.
arun (PM): thanks — if anyone has blockers ping me. we'll revisit in product sync on Thursday. :rocket:
